title: Internet Routing
short_description: Learn how data packets travel between computers through a network of interconnected routers while choosing efficient paths using Graph BFS, Graph DFS, Dijkstra's Algorithm, Floyd-Warshall and A* Pathfinding.

real_world_context.problem: Data packets need to travel between computers through a network of interconnected routers while choosing efficient paths. Network engineers must broadcast packets across the network, detect routing loops, find the lowest-latency path between any two routers, and choose the most efficient path using heuristic guidance.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Routing algorithms allow Internet service providers to deliver data efficiently across large router meshes, avoid loops, reduce latency, and keep the network responsive as it grows.

learning_objectives: Represent a router network as a graph using an adjacency list.
Broadcast a packet across the network with Breadth-First Search (BFS) and measure hops.
Detect routing loops with Depth-First Search (DFS).
Use Dijkstra's algorithm to find the lowest-latency path from a gateway to every router.
Use Floyd-Warshall to answer latency queries between every pair of routers.
Use A* pathfinding with a heuristic to find an efficient path between two routers.
prerequisites: Introduction to graphs and adjacency lists
completion_message: You have completed the Internet Routing mission. You have learned how graph traversal, shortest-path and heuristic-guided algorithms can be used to route data packets efficiently and reliably across an interconnected network of routers.
